A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tri-HE study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or merged material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Tri-HE evaluations, correlations with human judgments, hallucination mitigation experiments, and additional analyses and ablations in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports Llama-3.3 judge evaluations in Table 3 and benchmark annotation agreement in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds an alternative judge implementation using Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct in place of GPT-4. This is a limited model-component substitution: the judging prompt, triplet extraction, NLI procedure, and two-stage hallucination mitigation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GQA-derived Tri-HE benchmark with 300 images and 1,226 questions. The additional judge evaluation uses existing examples. Section 3.4 discusses other vision-language tasks as future work without evaluating them.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Llama-3.3 sentence-level and triplet-level judges alongside the retained NLI and GPT-4 comparisons. The evaluated LVLM set and LogicCheckGPT mitigation baseline are unchanged; InternLM2 is renamed InternLM-X2.

E3.justification: v3 reports a construction-quality assessment using three annotators on 100 common question-answer pairs and tests a 70B alternative judge on the existing Table 3 examples. Section 4 also changes the stated image-filter boundary from more than five relations to at least five; this does not establish that the dataset was rebuilt.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds a judge-backbone robustness analysis testing whether the triplet-versus-sentence findings persist with Llama-3.3. Response-length analysis, frequent-object-pair analysis, mitigation ablations, and qualitative comparisons already existed in v1; their relocation is not new evidence.

E5.justification: Section 4 newly reports a statistical reliability assessment of benchmark construction: Krippendorff's alpha of 0.62 for three annotators assessing 100 common question-answer pairs. The separate response-rating agreement of 0.66 remains unchanged. No repeated-run uncertainty or significance-testing procedure is added.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds 14 Llama-3.3 Pearson correlations, including 0.4705 for sentence-level and 0.5138 for triplet-level judging of LLaVA responses. Section 4 adds the 0.62 annotation-agreement result. Previously reported benchmark, judge-correlation, frequent-object-pair, ablation, and mitigation values are unchanged after matching the tables.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, distinctions between object hallucination, relation hallucination and prediction error, and HalluQ/HalluI equations are retained. The added generalizability discussion supplies conceptual explanation rather than new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 removes the prominent claim that mitigation achieves performance comparable to GPT-4V from the abstract, introduction, and contribution list. It retains the framework, benchmark, and mitigation contributions, including the claim of surpassing open-source competitors.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 explicitly conditions broader applicability on scene-graph availability and leaves other tasks for future evaluation. Section 5.3 interprets open-source judges as practical budget alternatives. Conversely, v1's explicit warning about possible bias from the 25-image and 20-image evaluation subsets disappears, although their sizes remain disclosed.

D1.justification: v3 provides explicit image-selection and annotation-verification criteria, identifies the Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct checkpoint, and adds a project page and an example configuration-repository pointer. The prompts, NLI threshold-selection procedure, default inference settings, and two-A100 hardware disclosure were already present in v1.

R1.justification: The Reefknot comparison shifts from emphasizing dataset contamination toward template restrictions and response-length bias. References add the InternLM-XComposer2 report, Llama-3.3, and several newer works, while removing Gemini. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The introductory motivation, dataset-construction account, and mitigation explanation are extensively rewritten. Earlier appendix material on threshold selection, object-pair ranking, response length, and mitigation is integrated into the main narrative, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. Judge terminology and citation style also change throughout.

P2.justification: The document adopts different typography, heading styles, and title/author layout throughout. Table 3 expands, v1 Tables 5 and 7 merge into v3 Table 5, and several plots and experimental tables move into the main text. Prompt figures are reordered and reformatted, while their substantive content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful additional validation through the Llama-3.3 comparison and construction-agreement assessment, explains annotation and mitigation procedures more clearly, and tempers the GPT-4V-parity claim. These are limited gains because the benchmark and existing results remain unchanged. Removing the explicit small-subset bias caveat weakens the limitations discussion, but the sample sizes remain visible and the additions support a modest net improvement.
